correctness.rationale: The projective incidence system is independently constructed in homogeneous and affine coordinates and compared under an explicit incidence isomorphism. Complete membership classification of all 8,192 point subsets agrees. The central directed exchange lemma is tested on all 3,995,862 distinct ordered pairs of transversal k-sets, k=6,...,13, by directly finding a legal targeted one-point substitution. Each substitution decreases Johnson distance exactly by one; induction proves exact geodesics. Independent BFS from all 702 six-set vertices reproduces 702 states, 7,488 edges, 468 degree-23/eccentricity-5 line-containing states, and 234 degree-18/eccentricity-6 line-free triangles; all radius/diameter values follow from the proven formula. No infinite extrapolation is made; executable source and output certificate are included.

The six-transversal family is not a matroid-basis family: the bundled checker verifies sets with masks 63 and 1182 and a fixed deletion of point index 0 for which no target point can be inserted to retain a line transversal. Therefore the full matroid basis exchange axiom fails, despite the weaker existence of some target-directed swap.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General reconfiguration statements were compared for logical strength: connectedness would not imply a shortest-possible Johnson route, and independent-set or matroid basis moves on different feasible families do not subsume the claimed projective-plane transversal identity. An explicit failure of the matroid basis-exchange axiom at k=6 excludes automatic deduction of these Johnson geodesics from the ordinary matroid basis theorem.

originality.rationale: The key new claim is exact target-directed exchange at every ordered pair of same-cardinality line-hitting subsets of PG(2,3) for k≥6, equivalently Johnson-graph isometry, with the sharp disconnected k=5 boundary. The static minimal-blocking-set classifications are explicitly disclaimed as novelty and do not imply path-length results; full available preprints of closest general reconfiguration sources differ in object and hypotheses. Eight actual public mathematical-record searches and topical scholarly searches found no equivalent or dominating claim. Inaccessible plausible full text is identified as a residual, nondecisive originality risk, rather than classified as negative evidence.
residual_risks: The complete 2022 Coolsaet–Botteldoorn–Fack paper could not be read; a hidden exchange-metric corollary in its body is not ruled out.
Some unindexed or unpublished computations of the same finite exchange graph might exist.
A stronger, unfamiliar general hitting-set geodesicity theorem might imply the result despite the targeted searches.

value.rationale: The theorem locates a sharp transition in an established geometric hitting-set problem: 13 disconnected K9 components at k=5 but uniform shortest-possible exchange paths for every pair at all k≥6. This is a stronger constraint than connectivity, is sensitive to the projective plane incidence geometry, and supplies an exact geodesic benchmark for transversal/token-jumping reconfiguration. Counts of static minimal blocking sets are not the claimed contribution. The six-transversal family violates strong matroid basis exchange, so the geodesicity is not an immediate generic matroid-basis consequence.
